fun_facts: Colston Loveland is from Gooding, Idaho.
Every April, Colston Loveland and his brothers helped brand cattle at their aunt and uncle’s farm—a job they liked because it meant skipping school.
Before becoming a Michigan national champion, Colston Loveland competed in rodeo.
In Michigan’s 2023 national championship game, Colston Loveland led the Wolverines with 64 receiving yards.
Colston Loveland scored his first Michigan touchdown against Ohio State and celebrated with a finger-to-lips gesture in front of 106,787 fans.
In 2024, Colston Loveland set a Michigan record for catches by a tight end with 56.

excerpts: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Two days before he was drafted with the 10th pick by the [Chicago Bears](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/chi/chicago-bears) , [Colston Loveland](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4723086/colston-loveland) was back home in Gooding, Idaho, branding cattle.

Every April, Loveland and his brothers venture down the road to their aunt and uncle's farm nestled in the southern Idaho town of 3,800 for an annual cattle branding. It's a job they'd do in groups to make for efficient work to brand, vaccinate and clip the ear of the calves. The tight end and his two brothers, Cayden and Cash, loved these days because it meant they got to skip school.

This rural backdrop -- what Loveland and others from Gooding refer to as a " [hidden gem](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hO_Fy7NdpOo) " -- was the setting for Loveland to evolve from competing in the rodeo to winning a national championship at Michigan to becoming a top-10 pick in
As a sophomore, Loveland was McCarthy's second-favorite weapon behind Roman Wilson and led the Wolverines in receiving yards (64) in the national championship game in 2023.

Loveland's first Michigan touchdown came on the road against Ohio State, where the Wolverines hadn't won since 2000 and trailed 20-17 early in the third quarter. ... After sprinting into the end zone, the freshman turned to the crowd of 106,787 and put his finger to his lips.

# 2025 NFL Draft: Bears select Michigan TE Colston Loveland with No. 10 overall pick

Published:

Updated:

body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nfl.com%2Fnews%2F2025-nfl-draft-bears-select-michigan-te-colston-loveland-with-no-10-overall-pick)

The Chicago Bears snagged a pass-catching tight end for Ben Johnson's offense.

With the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, the Bears selected Michigan's [Colston Loveland](https://www.nfl.com/prospects/colston-loveland/32004c4f-5645-6221-1f26-a303114b69f8) .

With the pick, Loveland became the highest TE drafted in the opening round by the Bears since legendary Hall of Famer Mike Ditka in 1961. Ditka was selected with the fifth overall pick. Greg Olsen, at No. 31 in 2007, is the only other tight end to be taken by the Bears in the first round.
